answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when overlapping behavior reveals duplicates. Like light through a prism, one operator's activity splits into many visible traces, and a shared audit graph compares timing, tool use, and counterparties. A velvet-smooth onboarding hides nothing once those traces overlap. Running ten fake sable identities then means locking ten stakes and risking all of them, so fakes cost real capital instead of just new names.
